title: EDIP: Commission adopts €1.5 billion work programme to boost European and Ukrainian defence industry
date_evidence: News article • 30 March 2026 • Directorate-General for Defence Industry and Space ... Publication date 30 March 2026
key_claim: The Commission adopted a €1.5 billion EDIP work programme for 2026-2027; more than €700 million supports the production increase of key defence components including counter-drone systems, missiles and ammunition (including €260 million via the Ukraine Support Instrument), with €325 million for European Defence Projects of Common Interest, €240 million for joint procurement, and €100 million in equity for start-ups and SMEs; EDIP was adopted on 8 December 2025 and the first calls open on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal from 31 March 2026.
notes: Tier 1 primary EU document (EC DG DEFIS news article). Anchors the headline that 2026 is the year the EU first puts dedicated EDIP money behind ammunition and components. The ec.europa.eu/presscorner mirror (IP/26/752) is JS-only and returned no body; the DG DEFIS news page carries the same content with a clean visible publication date.

title: 2026 EDIP Work Programme (Commission Implementing Decision C(2026) 2174 final)
key_claim: The EDIP work programme establishes a dedicated 'Energetic components' call (EDIP-P-2026-LS-IRA-EC) with a total budget of EUR 166 400 000 to reinforce EU industrial production capacity for energetic components including propellant powder (nitrocellulose; single, double and triple-base powder), explosives and access to relevant raw materials, with expected outcomes of tangible capacity increases in EU-based production and reduced single points of failure for energetic materials; a separate project allocates funds, coordinated by the European Defence Agency, to initiate harmonisation of national 155mm ammunition qualification processes toward a European qualification and certification system.
notes: Tier 1 primary EU legal act / work programme. The on-signal anchor: the EU is explicitly funding the energetics-feedstock chokepoint (propellant powder, nitrocellulose, access to raw materials). PDF read from EC server; title page carries the C(2026) 2174 final reference dated 30.3.2026.

title: Chemicals: Europe's Neglected Economic Security Frontier
key_claim: Europe's nitrocellulose demand for artillery propellants is estimated at around 20,000 tons annually but internal production is likely between 4,500 and 10,000 tons (led by Rheinmetall in Germany, Eurenco in France, and producers in Czechia and Poland); China controls roughly 46 percent of global chemical sales and, per Rheinmetall CEO Armin Papperger to the FT in April 2024, supplies more than 70 percent of Europe's cotton linters; the author argues rearmament strategies built on such supply chains are 'houses of cards', while Eurenco has restarted its Bergerac line and Poland is building a Grupa Azoty hub.
notes: Tier 2 institutional (DGAP / German Council on Foreign Relations; author Francesca Ghiretti, RAND Europe). Primary analytical anchor for the demand-vs-supply gap and the China feedstock dependency framing. Read directly from page; meta published_time confirms 26/03/2026.

publisher: Bruegel / Kiel Institute for the World Economy
title: Leading in spending, lagging in innovation: German defence procurement compared to the UK and Poland
date_evidence: Publishing date 12 May 2026 ... Published by the Kiel Institute for the World Economy as Kiel Report 8.
key_claim: In 2025 German military procurement reached roughly €85 billion and dominated European procurement (against about €25 billion in the UK and €21 billion in Poland), yet only about 12 percent of spending across the three countries went to new-paradigm systems; purchases from global suppliers fell sharply in 2025 and genuinely pan-European procurement remains extremely limited, 'pointing to fragmented industrial bases rather than a coordinated European rearmament effort', with delivery timelines typically two to four years.
verbatim_quote: pointing to fragmented industrial bases rather than a coordinated European rearmament effort
notes: Tier 2 institutional (Bruegel / Kiel Institute, Kiel Report 8). Used for the spending-surge-vs-capacity and fragmentation framing: record budgets are not buying coordinated industrial resilience. Read directly from Bruegel page; publishing date 12 May 2026.

title: Swedish, Polish firms invest in TNT plants to quench Europe's ammo thirst
key_claim: Sweden's Swebal is building the first TNT factory in Sweden since the Cold War, with capacity for more than 4,000 metric tons annually and production launching in 2028; Europe currently has only one major TNT plant, operated by Nitro-Chem in Poland, which signed a deal in March 2026 to open a second production unit; Russia is estimated to make more than 50,000 tons of TNT per year; the Swebal CEO warns that European producers depend on Asian energetic materials and that scaling final assembly is not enough because the entire raw-material supply chain must be scaled up.
verbatim_quote: there is only one such factory, operated by Nitro-Chem in Poland
notes: Tier 3 specialist trade press. Quantification anchor for TNT single-plant concentration, the Russia-Europe production asymmetry, and the upstream raw-material dependency. Read directly from page; visible byline 14 April 2026.

title: European Defence Agency to coordinate €50 million programme to harmonise 155mm ammunition testing
date_evidence: By Martin Chomsky (Defence Industry Europe) ... March 31, 2026
key_claim: The European Defence Agency will coordinate a new Joint Ammunition Qualification programme, funded with €50 million by the Commission under EDIP and focused initially on 155mm artillery ammunition; at present each Member State applies its own procedures to verify ammunition safety and performance, forcing manufacturers to repeat testing and certification in multiple countries, and the programme aims to introduce common procedures so ammunition tested in one Member State is accepted across others.
notes: Tier 3 trade press, corroborates the EDIP work-programme qualification project. Supports the disruption-pathway point that fragmented national qualification is itself a non-feedstock chokepoint. Read directly from page; visible byline 31 March 2026.

title: Europe's gunpowder bottleneck: how cotton supply chains became a defence issue
key_claim: Nitrocellulose, made from cotton linters, sits upstream of the artillery factory floor; Rheinmetall CEO Armin Papperger told the FT in April 2024 that Europe relies on China for 'more than 70 per cent' of its cotton linters; cotton-based feedstocks are not interchangeable on short notice because switching to wood pulp can trigger lengthy requalification of propellant formulations; China's tightened dual-use export controls took effect 1 December 2024; the US Treasury in May 2024 sanctioned cotton-cellulose and nitrocellulose suppliers including China-based entities; a June 2025 Jamestown assessment found Russian gunpowder production nearly doubled 2022-2024; and Rheinmetall acquired industrial nitrocellulose maker Hagedorn-NC in April 2025.
notes: Tier 3 specialist trade press. STRUCTURAL ANCHOR (3-6m band, 12/01/2026): the canonical framing piece tying the cotton-linter / nitrocellulose feedstock chokepoint, the requalification problem, and the China-dependency to Europe's ammunition ramp. Date read from page meta and visible byline.
